title: Iron
objective: After this level you can explain iron's role in steel and in your blood.
summary: Iron is the most abundant element in Earth as a whole and the most-used metal. A little carbon turns soft iron into steel. In your blood, iron sits in hemoglobin, which carries oxygen from your lungs.

cards.headline: The same element holds up bridges and carries oxygen in your blood.
cards.body: Iron is in the steel of skyscrapers and in every drop of your blood. How does one element manage both jobs?

cards.fact: Iron is the most abundant element in Earth as a whole: about 35 percent.
cards.context: Most of it is far out of reach, in the planet's core, which is made chiefly of iron. In the crust, iron comes fourth, at about 5 percent, after oxygen, silicon and aluminum. That's still plenty to go around: iron is the most-used and cheapest metal we have.

cards.headline: A pinch of carbon makes steel
cards.body: Pure iron is surprisingly soft. Add a little carbon, up to about 2 percent, and you get steel: far harder, and by far the most widely used material for building the world's infrastructure. Add more, 2 to 4 percent, and you get cast iron, which is brittle and weak when pulled. Level 33's carbon, in tiny amounts, turns a soft metal into the backbone of cities.

cards.headline: The iron in your blood
cards.body: Most of the iron in your body sits in hemoglobin, the protein in your blood that carries oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body. Remember Level 32: your cells combine oxygen with food to release energy. That oxygen has to reach them somehow, and iron is part of the delivery system. No iron, no delivery.

mascot.line: Same element in a bridge girder and in you. You're a little bit infrastructure.

questions.prompt: Iron is only about 5 percent of Earth's crust. How can it be the most abundant element in Earth as a whole?

options.label: Meteorites keep adding iron to the surface
Most of Earth's iron is in its core

The oceans are full of dissolved iron
